claim: *The decision move: the same arrow, a different mood.* A structural edge states that a call happens; a decision edge states that it is permitted. The absent edge carries the weight — "not allowed," not "does not happen" — and the analyses check a declared policy for consistency and least privilege.

topology.description: Parallel same-topology pair differs in edge meaning: observed fact vs permission.

required_terms: What is allowed, required or prohibited? Analyze rules, conflicts and consistency.
bw_encoding: Black outlines and arrows; white nodes; sparse 3–7% gray groups. Every non-solid relation is locally labeled; no distinction depends on color.
redesign: Native semantic redraw; colors replaced by labeled relations and line conventions.
alt: Two peer examples share a two-node topology. The descriptive edge says Service A calls B; the normative edge says Service A may call B. A separate crossed dashed arrow identifies an absent permission as not permitted. Text distinguishes observed fact from governing rule. The candidate uses black lines, white backgrounds and sparse gray; meaning does not depend on color.
